answer: Each agent registers one ferrous anchor chain, sized to its buoy depth, sable-marked, serial in a public registry. Auditors gauge an eighth per epoch; a chain whose sable mark misses by over 2% or whose serial appears twice burns its 70-credit bond. Buoys go shallowest first, so anchor chain k costs 25+8(k-1), and 1,000 fakes pay 4,021,000. A rented-chain ring fails: one chain cannot sit at two buoys at once. An honest agent pays 25 once.
